## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uragapetavatthu* ("The Snake", Pv 12) is a verse text in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Its theme concerns overcoming grief, addressing whether it is possible to remain free of sorrow when someone dies, an attainment ascribed to noble disciples of the Buddha [SuttaCentral]. In studies on the chronology of the Pali Canon, the text is noted in the context of verse sharing and borrowing between the *Petavatthu* and the *Jātaka* collection [Kingsbury 2002].

Text-reuse analysis reflects extensive connections between this text and the *Jātaka* tradition. SuttaCentral cross-references the *Uragapetavatthu* directly with the *Uragajātaka* (Ja 354) [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with this, DharmaNexus detects 8 matching segments shared with the *Uragajātaka* (Ja 354), including an extensive parallel spanning segments §0.2–11.1 at 0.96 similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial Pali-internal text reuse with three commentarial works: 45 matching passages in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match at §7.4–9.2), 12 matches in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, and 6 matches in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan meet the detection threshold [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
